When a battery degrades to roughly 70–80% of its original capacity, it is typically no longer suitable for vehicle use, but it retains considerable capacity for stationary storage applications — for example, storing energy from solar panels or providing backup power to buildings. Several automotive manufacturers have partnered with energy companies to deploy repurposed EV batteries in large-scale grid storage projects. Before reuse, however, operators must estimate a pack's remaining health and trace how it was used. Testing, transport, disassembly and liability all affect whether a second-life project is economical.
